cards.title: Edit Elementor sections with device-specific padding
cards.summary: Use Elementor's per-device padding controls and the mobile-only icon indicator to fix section spacing differently on mobile, tablet and desktop.
cards.use_when: Tuning store homepage, PDP or landing-page section spacing in Elementor so content isn't cut off or crammed on mobile while staying correct on desktop.
steps: Select the section by clicking its six-dot handle, then open the Advanced tab to reach padding controls.
Watch for the small device icon next to a control: if the icon is present the change applies only to that device; if it is absent the change is global across all breakpoints.
Add padding around the section, unlink the values, and push extra padding to the top to move content down away from the header.
Switch the editor viewport (desktop / tablet / mobile) and repeat the adjustment for each device that needs different spacing.
Also edit individual widgets per device — buttons, headings and image widgets each have their own responsive controls.
Click Publish to save, then use the preview (eyeball) icon to check the live rendering before moving on.
caveats: Remember the device icon rule: a global edit will overwrite the value on every breakpoint, so make global changes first and device-specific ones after.
If a section is disabled for desktop it won't render there at all — verify the correct breakpoint before assuming a layout is broken.

cards.title: Center misaligned Elementor widgets per breakpoint
cards.summary: Fix widgets that sit off to the left on mobile by setting their Style > Position to center within the mobile-only viewport.
cards.use_when: Correcting a call-to-action button, heading or image on a store landing page that looks left-aligned or off-center on phones after template import.
steps: Switch the Elementor viewport to the device you want to fix (start with mobile).
Click the widget (for example the button) and open the Style tab, then find the Position setting.
Confirm the mobile device icon is showing next to the control before changing it, so the edit is scoped to that breakpoint only.
Set the position to center.
Switch back to desktop view — the widget automatically returns to its original alignment (for example left) because the change was mobile-scoped.
Repeat the same operation in tablet view, then Publish and preview.
caveats: If the device icon is not present, the alignment change will apply to all breakpoints — check before saving.
Responsive overrides only behave as expected if the original desktop layout was left intact.

cards.title: Launch a WooCommerce store by switching from coming-soon to live
cards.summary: Take the WordPress/WooCommerce site out of store-coming-soon mode and save changes so shoppers can actually buy.
cards.use_when: Final go-live step after building and previewing a WooCommerce store, when checkout and product pages need to be publicly reachable.
steps: Finish all page building, responsive edits and content replacement, and Publish your work in the builder.
Preview the site with the eyeball icon to confirm layout, images, copy and store pages look correct on desktop and mobile.
Locate the store's coming-soon indicator/notice and click it to open the setting.
Change the status from Coming Soon to Live.
Save changes.
Verify on a logged-out browser or incognito window that product pages and checkout are reachable to the public.
caveats: Don't switch to Live before testing checkout, payments and shipping settings — going live exposes the store immediately.
Preview inside the editor is not the same as a public visit; confirm from an incognito session.

cards.title: Customise an imported template by replacing images, colours and text
cards.summary: Build a store page faster by starting from a template and swapping images, text and colours rather than designing from scratch.
cards.use_when: Building a store homepage, category page or landing page quickly when a template already provides the section structure.
steps: Add or open the desired section and drop in an Image widget via the Add Element panel.
Replace the placeholder image by selecting the image control and choosing the desired file from the media library.
Overwrite placeholder copy with your own product, category or brand text.
Change the template's accent colours in Style settings so the page matches your brand palette.
Adjust spacing and alignment per device (see responsive padding/position cards) after swapping content, because template spacing rarely fits your assets.
Publish and preview to confirm the swapped assets render correctly.
caveats: Template images and copy may carry licensing/branding constraints — replace them before going live.
Swapping content often breaks the original spacing, so always re-check padding and alignment afterwards.
